cases.title: Crypto Income
cases.summary: Trump’s annual disclosure records about $1.42 billion across selected crypto royalty, token and equity-sale proceeds. The strongest direct ownership link is CIC Digital: $635.1 million in royalties in a company wholly owned by the trust of which Trump is sole beneficiary. These are identifiable business receipts, with mixed family ownership in other entities; they are not a verified personal net-profit total.
cases.qualification: The payment-level reconciliation between Aryam’s full consideration and the two disclosed equity proceeds, plus individual distributions and taxes.

cases.title: Foreign Fees
cases.summary: Kushner’s private-equity firm earns management fees from foreign investors while he undertakes diplomacy for his father-in-law. Garcia and Wyden estimated more than $60 million in 2025 fees, including $39 million from Saudi investors. That is a concrete estimate of revenue to the business he owns, not a $2 billion personal gift.
cases.evidence_status: Estimated firm fees; personal distributions undisclosed
cases.qualification: Annual investor-by-investor cash fees, expense deductions, Kushner distributions, and dated conflict-management records; these would turn the current revenue estimate into a reconciled personal-benefit figure.

cases.title: Family Capital
cases.summary: 1789 Capital, where Donald Trump Jr. is a partner, invested in Vulcan shortly before the government announced a $620 million loan commitment for the magnet producer. The public financing can increase the value of a private investment, but the loan is owed by the company; it is not a $620 million payment to Trump Jr.
cases.qualification: 1789’s Vulcan stake, Trump Jr.’s partnership ownership and carried interest, loan disbursements, decision chronology and conflict reviews.

cases.title: Stock Income
cases.summary: Nancy Pelosi's 2025 annual disclosure reports more than $7 million in income from three spouse-owned stock positions: Apple, Amazon and Nvidia. The filing puts the family's financial interest in major technology companies on the record while she served in Congress.
cases.qualification: Political causation, insider trading, exact net after-tax profit, or that the issuers transferred the entire reported gains to the family.

cases.title: Foreign Payments
cases.summary: Federal prosecutors accused Henry and Imelda Cuellar of receiving roughly $600,000 through arrangements involving an Azerbaijani state-owned energy company and a Mexican bank. The indictment described payments routed through the wife's companies in exchange for official favors. Both denied wrongdoing and received presidential pardons before trial.
cases.qualification: A verdict that the Cuellars took bribes, a new FY2023–FY2026 payment total, or an exact personal-profit allocation.

cases.title: Cash & Gold
cases.summary: A senator, his wife and businessmen formed a network that exchanged money and valuables for political influence. Robert and Nadine Menendez were separately convicted. Their case shows the full chain: a family intermediary, a foreign-backed business advantage, private benefits and official intervention.
cases.qualification: That the historical seizure is new income inside FY2023–FY2026, or that every dollar of a foreign company's revenue flowed to the couple.

cases.title: Family Contracts
cases.summary: Federal ethics investigators traced nearly $1 million in munitions contracts to companies owned by Rep. Cory Mills after he entered Congress. His wife held leadership roles in the businesses. The record connects the officeholder, family, corporate ownership and federal buyers without pretending the full contract value became personal income.
cases.evidence_status: Documented company awards / formal ethics referral
cases.qualification: A final legal violation, the family's exact retained profit, or the assumption that nearly $1 million in corporate awards equals nearly $1 million in household cash.

cases.title: Wall Contracts
cases.summary: Fisher Sand & Gravel recorded $13.35 billion in FY2026 net federal contract obligations. Its family leadership and documented political access make the allocation of those contracts a concrete accountability question.
cases.evidence_status: Documented awards; reported access; disputed procurement
qualification: Do not present aggregate national wall mileage as Fisher-specific completion.
Do not assert a current final disposition of the May 2026 lawsuit; later docket outcome was not independently established in this bounded review.
Do not claim campaign funds were recycled from these contracts without a traced money path.
Do not replace company obligations with personalcash or compute family profit using an assumed margin.
